      Introduction: About World Investment Report

                    It is an annual flagship publication by the UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

                    It analyzes global and regional trends in foreign direct investment (FDI).

                    It provides data on multinational enterprises, evaluates investment policies, and offers
             policy recommendations to help developing countries harness investment for
            sustainable growth.

          Core Focus Areas

               FDI Tracking: Measures global, regional, and national foreign direct investment
               flows and structural shifts.

              Corporate Rankings: Lists the world’s largest transnational corporations.

             Thematic Analysis: Focuses a deep-dive study each year on a critical topic, such
              as the digital economy or sustainable development goals.

                Policy Guidance: Evaluates national and international regulatory changes,
               investment incentives, and screening measures

     Key Highlights of World Investment Report 2026

          Title: International Investment in a Turbulent Era Overview

     Global trends and prospects





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            1

Global Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) remained
                                                                         resilient in 2025, with modest growth despite
                                                                  geopolitical tensions, trade policy uncertainty,
           Overall Status (Global FDI Trends – 2025)        and high financing costs. However, investment
                                                became increasingly concentrated across a few
                                                  economies and sectors, while underlying
                                                          investment conditions remained fragile.

                                                            Global FDI flows increased by 6% to US$1.6
                                                                              trillion in 2025. Excluding conduit flows through
          Global FDI Flows
                                                         major European financial centres, FDI rose by
                                              4%, following two consecutive years of decline.

                                                  The increase in FDI was mainly driven by
                                                                financial centres, investment hubs, and stronger
           Drivers of Growth                                 inflows into a limited number of large economies,
                                                                rather than broad-based global investment
                                                           growth.

                                                          Investment became more selective and
                                                         concentrated, with the top 20 host economies
          Investment Concentration
                                                         accounting for over 80% of global FDI inflows in
                                                     2025.

                                                  The top 20 host economies consisted equally of
                                                     developed and developing economies, although
         Top FDI Recipients
                                                            the overall composition changed only marginally
                                                       from previous years.

                                                         FDI growth was concentrated in capital- and
                                                          technology-intensive sectors, particularly digital
           Sectoral Distribution
                                                                infrastructure, semiconductors, and selected
                                                          energy-related industries.

                                                  The value of cross-border mergers and
                                                             acquisitions (M&As) declined by 7%, indicating
          Cross-Border Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A)
                                                    weaker international corporate investment despite
                                                            strong domestic deal activity.

                                                           Greenfield project announcements remained
                                                           broadly unchanged from 2024, supported mainly
          Greenfield Investments
                                                    by large-scale projects in data centres, oil & gas,
                                                   and semiconductors.

                                                               International project finance recovered
                                                           modestly, with project values increasing by 3% in
           International Project Finance                   2025, ending a three-year decline. However,
                                                           values remained about 25% below the 2021
                                                        peak, while the number of deals continued to fall.





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            2

FDI remained the largest source of external
                                                         finance for developing countries, accounting for
         Importance for Developing Economies           about half of total external financing, ahead of
                                                           remittances, Official Development Assistance
                                                        (ODA), and portfolio investment.

                                                         FDI contributes to productive capacity,
                                                       technology transfer, employment generation,
         Developmental Role of FDI                    and integration into Global Value Chains (GVCs),
                                                     making it a critical driver of long-term economic
                                                        development.

                                                         FDI inflows to Least Developed Countries (LDCs)
          FDI in Vulnerable Economies                     increased by 21% in 2025, but remained
                                                         concentrated in a few resource-rich economies.

                                                         FDI in Small Island Developing States (SIDS)
                                                       remained modest and was concentrated mainly in
          Small Island Developing States (SIDS)
                                                            tourism, renewable energy, and logistics
                                                               sectors.

                                                  The persistently low share of FDI in LDCs reflects
                                                           challenges such as small domestic markets,
          Challenges for LDCs
                                                         higher investment risks, limited infrastructure,
                                                   and weak integration into high-growth sectors.

                                                  The outlook for 2026 remains highly uncertain,
                                                             with significant downside risks arising from
          FDI Outlook for 2026                           slower global economic growth, trade policy
                                                            uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and ongoing
                                                                      conflicts.

                                                               Rising uncertainty may lead multinational
                                                              enterprises to delay, cancel, or suspend
          Risks to Investment
                                                       investment projects, resulting in weaker
                                                            productive investment.

                                                          Strong profits and healthy balance sheets of
                                                             leading multinational enterprises (MNEs) may
                                                              sustain investment in high-value industries, but
          Role of Multinational Enterprises (MNEs)
                                                         could further concentrate global FDI across a
                                                                    limited number of countries and technology-
                                                            intensive sectors.

     Regional Trends

           Overall Regional Trends (2025)                  FDI inflows increased in both developed and
                                                       developing economies, but growth remained
                                                    uneven across regions. Investment continued to





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            3

be concentrated in a limited number of countries,
                                                               sectors, and large-scale projects.

                                                         FDI inflows to developed economies increased
         Developed Economies                        by 11% to approximately US$723 billion in 2025,
                                                                  largely driven by Europe.

                                                     Growth in Europe was supported by financial
                                                         centres and investment hubs, while the
         Europe                                     European Union (EU) witnessed strong cross-
                                                       border M&A activity and major investment
                                                                  projects, particularly in France and Germany.

                                                         FDI inflows to North America remained broadly
                                                                   stable, supported by investments in strategic
          North America                                     industries, although weaker cross-border M&A
                                                   and project finance activity limited overall
                                                           growth.

                                                         FDI inflows to other developed economies
          Other Developed Economies                    remained broadly stable, with investment focused
                                                   on high-value sectors.

                                                  The value of greenfield projects increased
                                                             despite a decline in the number of projects,
          Greenfield Investment in Developed Economies
                                                                 indicating fewer but larger capital-intensive
                                                         investments.

                                                        Major investments were concentrated in
                                                       semiconductors, data centres, clean energy,
         Key Investment Sectors (Developed Economies)
                                                           battery manufacturing, and advanced
                                                        manufacturing.

                                                         FDI inflows to developing economies increased
          Developing Economies                        by 2% to US$901 billion in 2025, with significant
                                                               regional variations.

                                                       Developing Asia remained the largest FDI
          Developing Asia                                   recipient among developing regions, receiving
                                             US$644 billion in inflows.

                                                         FDI declined in East Asia, including China, but
          Regional Trends within Asia                      increased in South-East Asia, South Asia, West
                                                              Asia, and Central Asia.

                                                       South-East Asia emerged as the largest FDI-
          South-East Asia
                                                           receiving subregion within developing Asia.

                                                               India drove strong investment growth in South
           India's Performance                               Asia, with FDI inflows increasing by 44% in
                                                     2025.





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            4

Eight of the top ten developing-economy FDI
          FDI Concentration in Asia                         recipients were located in Developing Asia,
                                                                  highlighting the region's dominant position.

                                                         FDI inflows into Africa stood at US$70 billion in
                                                     2025, lower than the exceptional US$94 billion in
           Africa
                                                    2024, which had been boosted by a few very
                                                                large investment deals.

                                                           Despite the annual decline, Africa's inflows
                                                       remained about one-third above the 2010–2024
           Africa's Long-Term Performance
                                                     average and represented the third-highest level
                                                         since 1990.

                                                         While the value of greenfield projects declined
                                                    by nearly one-third, the number of projects
          Investment Pattern in Africa
                                                           increased, indicating broader participation
                                                         through smaller investments.

                                                          Investment remained concentrated in energy
         Key Sectors in Africa                               infrastructure, extractive industries, renewable
                                                         energy, and critical minerals.

                                                         FDI inflows increased by 14% to US$188 billion,
           Latin America & the Caribbean (LAC)              driven primarily by strong investment in South
                                                       America, especially Brazil.

                                                  The top 10 recipient economies accounted for
          Investment Concentration in LAC           95% of total regional FDI inflows, indicating high
                                                          geographical concentration.

                                                           Despite higher FDI inflows, the value of
                                                 announced greenfield projects declined by
          Greenfield Projects in LAC                     about one-third to less than US$120 billion,
                                                           mainly due to reduced investment in
                                                      manufacturing and logistics.

                                                         FDI inflows to Least Developed Countries
                                                          (LDCs), Landlocked Developing Countries
           Structurally Weak & Vulnerable Economies       (LLDCs), and Small Island Developing States
                                                           (SIDS) remained limited, volatile, and highly
                                                         concentrated.

                                                         FDI inflows to LDCs increased to US$43 billion,
          Least Developed Countries (LDCs)
                                                         accounting for 2.7% of global FDI flows.

         Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDCs)        FDI inflows to LLDCs declined by 2% in 2025.

                                                         FDI inflows to SIDS increased by 4%, although
          Small Island Developing States (SIDS)            investment levels remained well below
                                                      development requirements.





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            5

Investment in LDCs, LLDCs, and SIDS remained
                                                         concentrated in a few resource-rich economies,
           Sectoral Focus in Vulnerable Economies
                                                             with limited diversification beyond renewable
                                                     energy and logistics.

      Sectoral highlights

                                                     Growth in greenfield investment and
                                                               international project finance was concentrated in
           Overall Sectoral Trends (2025)                 a few technology-driven sectors, particularly
                                                                      digital infrastructure, while most other sectors
                                                        experienced declining investment activity.

                                                           Greenfield investment in digital infrastructure
            Digital Infrastructure                            increased by more than 80%, primarily driven by
                                                              large-scale investments in data centres.

                                                          Investment values also increased in
                                                     semiconductors and oil & gas, although growth
         Semiconductors & Oil and Gas
                                               was significantly smaller compared to digital
                                                                    infrastructure.

                                                   Most sectors witnessed significant declines in
                                                        both greenfield investment and international
          Decline in Other Sectors                          project finance, including renewable energy,
                                                           transport infrastructure, and Global Value Chain
                                                         (GVC)-intensive manufacturing.

                                                  Announced greenfield investment in GVC-
                                                            intensive manufacturing industries declined by
          GVC-Intensive Manufacturing
                                                   13%, reflecting global policy uncertainty and
                                                       ongoing supply chain restructuring.

                                                             Greenfield investment in electronics (excluding
                                                      semiconductors) fell by nearly 40%,
           Electronics Sector
                                                            representing one of the sharpest sectoral
                                                                declines.

                                                  Announced investment in the automotive sector
         Automotive Industry                             declined by around 25%, reflecting weaker global
                                                         manufacturing investment.

                                                          Investment in textiles, clothing, and leather
                                                             industries decreased by about 30%, indicating
            Textiles, Clothing & Leather
                                                          continued challenges for labour-intensive
                                                         manufacturing sectors.

          Investment in SDG-Related Sectors               Investment linked to the Sustainable
                                                   Development Goals (SDGs) recovered during





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            6

2025, particularly in Least Developed Countries
                                                          (LDCs), although progress remained uneven
                                                         across sectors, countries, and investment modes.

                                                                      In developing countries, the value of greenfield
          Developing Countries                          investment projects increased by 11%, while
                                                               international project finance grew by 26%.

                                                  The recovery in SDG-related investment was
                                                             driven mainly by increased investment in the
         Telecommunications
                                                      telecommunications sector, reflecting growing
                                               demand for digital connectivity.

                                                         While renewable energy investment slowed
                                                         across developing countries overall, both
         Renewable Energy
                                                       investment value and project numbers increased
                                                                        in LDCs, albeit from a relatively low base.

                                                          Investment in other SDG-related sectors,
                                                               including transport, water and sanitation, health,
         Lagging SDG Sectors
                                                   and education, continued to lag, particularly in
                                                        terms of the number of new projects.

                                                  The recovery in sustainable development
                                                          investment remained uneven across sectors,
         Uneven Recovery                                 countries, and investment modes, limiting
                                                          progress toward achieving the Sustainable
                                                     Development Goals.

     Major investor trends

                                                  The global Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)
                                                        landscape is becoming increasingly diversified,
                                                             with traditional Multinational Enterprises (MNEs)
           Overall Investor Trends (2025)
                                                         being joined by State-owned MNEs (SO-MNEs)
                                                   and private equity investors as major sources of
                                                                   international investment.

                                                          Alongside private multinational corporations,
                                                    State-owned enterprises and private equity
         Changing FDI Landscape
                                                     funds are playing a growing role in cross-border
                                                             investment, reshaping global FDI patterns.

                                                  The top 100 non-financial MNEs are increasingly
                                                      dominated by firms operating in strategic sectors
         Top 100 Non-Financial MNEs
                                                     such as technology and pharmaceuticals,
                                                                   reflecting shifting global investment priorities.

         Technology & Pharmaceutical Sectors           Technology and pharmaceutical MNEs
                                                   expanded their foreign assets by more than 10%




World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            7

in 2025, strengthening their position among the
                                                             world's largest multinational enterprises.

                                                     Over the past decade, East Asian and other
                                                       developing economy MNEs have become among
         Emergence of East Asian MNEs
                                                            the fastest internationalizing firms, measured by
                                                            the share of foreign assets in their total assets.

                                                        Rapid international expansion of developing-
                                                          country MNEs has been concentrated in
         Key Growth Sectors
                                                         technology, manufacturing, infrastructure, and
                                                     renewable energy sectors.

                                                    State-owned multinational enterprises have
                                                          regained importance in international investment
          Rise of State-Owned MNEs (SO-MNEs)            following the COVID-19 pandemic, reflecting a
                                                              greater role of governments in strategic
                                                            investments.

                                                    State-owned MNEs account for more than one-
                                                          quarter of the top 100 global MNEs and half of
         Share of State-Owned MNEs
                                                         the leading MNEs based in developing
                                                     economies.

                                                      State-owned MNEs increasingly undertake cross-
                                                       border acquisitions through investment
          Cross-Border Acquisitions                       consortia involving private investors and
                                                                   institutional investors, contributing significantly
                                                                  to global FDI flows.

                                                             Private equity has emerged as a major channel
           Private Equity Investment                            for international investment, expanding its role in
                                                               global mergers and acquisitions.

                                                                      In 2025, cross-border private equity
                                                           transactions reached nearly US$200 billion,
          Cross-Border Private Equity Transactions
                                                                  highlighting the growing importance of private
                                                                   capital in international investment.

                                                                   International private equity acquisitions
                                                      accounted for approximately 20% of global
          Role in Global M&A
                                                        cross-border mergers and acquisitions (M&A) in
                                                     2025.

                                                        Although developing economies receive only a
                                                             small share of global private equity investment,
           Private Equity in Developing Economies           inflows are concentrated in technology and other
                                                      high-growth sectors, supporting innovation and
                                                    economic expansion.





World Investment Report 2026                                                                                                            8

Increased investment by private equity funds
                                                   and technology-focused MNEs provides
          Innovation & Growth                               opportunities for innovation, technology
                                                                 transfer, productivity growth, and expansion of
                                                            high-value industries in developing countries.
